blocks.hero_h1: Toyota HiAce 2023–2026 import NZ for business
blocks.hero_subtitle: The 2023–2026 HiAce range is worth a proper look if you need a van or people mover with the right body configuration. We can search Japanese auctions for Super GL Dark Prime II van and Grand Cabin wagon variants, then confirm the exact model code, seating, fuel type and import viability before any bid.
proof_points: Japan auction access for customer-approved bids
Importing Estimate, compliance is part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: NZ buyers consider the HiAce because the body style matters as much as the badge: Super GL Dark Prime II suits business use with a more finished cabin, while Grand Cabin suits passenger work with 10 seats. The scoped imports include GDH206V 2.8 diesel AWD, GDH201V 2.8 diesel RWD, TRH229W 2.7 petrol AWD and TRH224W 2.7 petrol RWD, so the right choice depends on load, seating and where the van will spend its working week. Cargo space, payload needs and condition should be matched to the exact listing, especially if you are weighing a Japan auction vehicle against NZ ex-fleet vans. If diesel dependability is your reason for looking, the auction list still needs to support the exact van's mileage, grade and notes.
blocks.video_caption: A walkaround should show the door layout, rear access and cabin layout clearly. On a HiAce, those details tell you more about day-to-day use than the badge on the tailgate.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The useful part of importing a HiAce is choice. Within the 2023–2026 scope you can target the van body, the wagon body, diesel or petrol, and RWD or AWD depending on the model code. Before bidding we check the exact auction car, translate the auction list information available, and explain the grade, mileage, recorded notes, modifications and likely landed-cost position without pretending the listing proves more than it does. For business buyers worried about downtime, previous commercial use or corrosion under panels, we point out only what is recorded on the auction list or visible in the supplied photos.

buyer_persona.headline: Best suited for:
buyer_persona.body: This page is aimed at business owners, shuttle operators, camper-conversion buyers and families who need more space than an SUV. If you care about the exact body, seating and drivetrain rather than just buying the first HiAce you see, importing is a solid match.

standout_features_block.headline: Features that stand out
standout_features_block.intro: The HiAce details that matter are practical ones: body format, seating and the exact grade fitted to the auction car.

items.title: Super GL Dark Prime II van grade
items.body: Super GL Dark Prime II is the requested van edition in this import brief. The exact trim equipment still needs to be confirmed on the auction list for each car.

items.title: Grand Cabin 10-seat wagon layout
items.body: The Grand Cabin variants in this scope are 10-seat petrol wagons, aimed at passenger carrying rather than trade cargo. That makes the TRH229W and TRH224W a different buy from a Super GL van.
items.image_hint: Side door open with passenger rows visible inside the cabin

items.title: Van and Grand Cabin wagon body choice
items.body: This HiAce import brief separates Super GL van and Grand Cabin wagon forms. That is useful because registration use, seating and conversion plans depend on the exact body type, not just the HiAce name.
items.image_hint: Rear quarter view showing van body proportions and rear access

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The safest way to buy a HiAce is to tie each powertrain claim to the exact model code.

items.title: 2.8 diesel van codes
items.body: The supplied import brief maps GDH206V to the 2.8 diesel AWD van and GDH201V to the 2.8 diesel RWD van. Both are within the requested Super GL Dark Prime II scope. That split matters for a business buyer because drivetrain affects traction, running costs and what you should compare before bidding.

items.title: 2.7 petrol wagon codes
items.body: The supplied import brief maps TRH229W to the 2.7 petrol AWD wagon and TRH224W to the 2.7 petrol RWD wagon. Both are within the requested Grand Cabin scope, with 10 seats confirmed for the current Grand Cabin wagon specification.

items.title: 2023–2026 range timing
items.body: This page covers the 2023–2026 HiAce period. Toyota’s 2025 Japan news release says HiAce Van and Wagon models were part of a partial improvement launched on 1 July 2025. For a buyer, that means a 2025 or 2026 auction car should be checked carefully by exact model code and listing details rather than treated as identical to an earlier example.

models_comparison.intro: Use this as a model-code guide rather than a promise about any single auction car.

rows.notes: Checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding; final certification occurs in NZ.

Super GL Dark Prime II is the van-focused grade in this brief; Grand Cabin is the 10-seat wagon option. These two forms suit different commercial, passenger and conversion uses.

blocks.how_to_use_iyc: Send us the year range, budget, preferred body type and any must-have model codes such as GDH206V, GDH201V, TRH229W or TRH224W. We search current Japanese auction options, translate the auction list information available, explain the landed-cost estimate and place a live bid only after you approve the vehicle and bid limit.

faq_block.q: Can you search for a specific HiAce model code?
faq_block.a: Yes. The key codes in this import brief are GDH206V, GDH201V, TRH229W and TRH224W. We confirm the exact code, grade, seating and drivetrain from the auction information before you decide on a bid.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the landed estimate?
faq_block.a: The Importing Estimate uses the approved landed-cost breakdown and is calculated from live auction examples and the exchange rate at the time. Compliance and on-road costs remain variable until they are confirmed for the exact vehicle.

faq_block.q: Can you confirm NZ compliance before bidding?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding; final certification occurs in NZ. We support the process, but we do not promise the result before the vehicle is assessed.

faq_block.q: How long does the import process take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when the right vehicle is purchased, vessel space, customs processing and NZ entry certification. We update you through the purchase, shipping and arrival steps.

faq_block.q: What do you review on the auction list?
faq_block.a: We translate and explain the auction list information supplied for the car, including grade, odometer, condition notes, damage markings, listed modifications and any records supplied. Photos and supporting information vary between listings.

blocks.company_positioning: ImportYourCar.co.nz is a NZ-based import service operated by Ultimate Motors Ltd, helping buyers source vehicles from Japanese auctions since 2009. Our role is auction access, pricing guidance, auction-list explanation, bidding support and coordination through purchase, shipping, customs and NZ arrival.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this is not for
items: If you need a van ready for work immediately, waiting for the right auction car, shipping and NZ entry certification will not suit.
If you do not know whether you need the Super GL van or Grand Cabin wagon configuration, sort that out before bidding because the wrong body type is an expensive mismatch.
If your plan involves conversion work or passenger service, registration use and compliance details need to be checked before you approve a car.

alternatives_block.intro: These are the closest researched alternatives if the HiAce brief changes.

rows.better_if: You want a close Japanese-market rival to the HiAce for commercial, passenger or camper-conversion use.
rows.tradeoff: Specification, resale demand and parts preferences may differ from the Toyota HiAce in New Zealand.

rows.better_if: You want a more passenger-focused Toyota van with a higher-comfort interior rather than a work van base.
rows.tradeoff: Less suited to cargo or trade use and likely a different buyer budget from mainstream HiAce variants.

engine_drivetrain_block.headline: HiAce powertrain choices to confirm
engine_drivetrain_block.body: For the 2023–2026 HiAce scope, the van and wagon branches need to be kept separate. Use the technical code mapping above to separate the 2.8 diesel Super GL Dark Prime II van variants from the 2.7 petrol Grand Cabin wagon variants before comparing any auction car.

savings_block.headline: How the landed cost is calculated
savings_block.body: We calculate the estimate for the exact vehicle before you bid. It includes the vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, shipping costs, compliance, on-road costs and customs clearance. Compliance and on-road costs vary by vehicle, so they are confirmed in the current estimate rather than presented as fixed amounts.
